how: A flag proposal with anchor coordinates and dimensions gives other members a shared work to join.
Calls recruit members to guard the national flag and gather defenders through social networks.
A request for black-line work receives a bare commitment rather than a negotiated exchange.
Members limit expansion because they judge their available defenders insufficient.
Members contest which national symbols and jokes belong beside the flag.
Members report individual contributions and corrections while construction continues.
Coordinates, dimensions and requests for numbered axes make a common target usable.
A shared image guides reported bot operation and recruits spare accounts into an automated pool.
Decisions made in chat return as public target changes that participants can follow.
Revised plans need accessible announcements because lurkers otherwise miss changes and defend against their own revisions.
Public coordination remains necessary for participants who cannot access the chat or cannot find its official server.
Changing a shared design requires aligning active bot targets or participants may fight their own automated maintenance.
Claims of unlimited timerless painting require verification because several apparent workarounds affect only the local display.

statement: Testing whether apparent extra pixels reach the shared canvas
how: Participants check apparent exploits against shared results and abandon claims that succeed only in the client.
Local divisions and votes coexist with repeated requests for leadership, so no overall commander cannot mean no decided order.
Separate requested sanctions from enforced exclusions and from corrected accusations before treating policing as decided order.

statement: Disputing which recruits the room will admit
how: Calls for more hands provoke disputes over admitting potential helpers from an already disparaged outside venue.
Guard calls, study between placements and sleep handovers turn maintenance into continuing labour.
Candidate attribution work is needed to distinguish sabotage from mistakes, delayed usernames and planned resizing.
A displayed username is insufficient evidence of a bad pixel when attribution and colour updates lag.
An explanation of a mistaken tile can reverse blame through apology and acceptance.
Participants seek truces, specify mutual defence and hold neighbours to claimed agreements.
Members refuse attacks because targets are allies or because bothering another country's work is unwarranted.
Requests receive conditional help, reciprocal night cover or postponement according to available capacity.
Named alliances, reciprocal watch across sleeping hours and a shared heart join the work of several rooms.
Members carry truce proposals and alliance outreach between rooms.
The tentative process is locally evidenced as limited representation, while an actual dispute over binding every placer remains unobserved.
The explicit Tango relocation responds to incumbent builders rather than a recorded erasure or overrun.
Negotiating an occupied site can produce a preventive move published through a replacement plan.
Requests to build below another flag or borrow white space do not reveal continuing residence under a host's rules.
Established national and sporting rivalries supply names and taunts for canvas antagonists.
National history, political memes and locally born jokes give canvas additions meanings beyond the flag.
Some attack-related turns explicitly invoke national history or sporting rivalry to name the target.
Participants identify borrowed subreddit styling and performed national identities as an April Fools joke.
Canvas saturation prompts objections, defences of its worth and demands to contain posts.
Containment requests and a reported sweep do not establish the scope or implementation of a moderator posting rule.

statement: Continuing ordinary room life beside the canvas
how: A retained random thread sustains meetup concerns, graduation, study and relationship talk alongside canvas arguments.
Ordinary formats can persist while losing attention to canvas hype, so host displacement is selective rather than total.
Completion reports elicit pride and credit for what members made together.
Participants preserve timelapses, recount repairs and mourn allied losses after the ending.
Members propose successor canvases and promise a return while other participants demand an end to posting.
A continuation proposal remains unresolved without visible acceptance or action, especially when replies reject it.
The tentative process is supported only as editing and preservation because the retained concepts show no contest over keeping historical damage.
Attack calls and reports include invasion, converting a rival flag and repeated provocative alterations.
Members extend the contest through rival-chat heckling, sporting taunts and victory claims.
Accusations about a whole room require separate attribution because participants contest personal involvement and collective blame.
Starting and calling for hands may be accomplished in the same proposal rather than separate sequential acts.
A concrete line-building call receives a member's report that they are joining the work.
The local call receives a bare acceptance, but neither silence nor this pair establishes an obligation or preference for every reader.
Participants explicitly answer the canvas posting flood by requesting fewer posts and one shared channel.
A shared image can settle one target without ending disagreements over revisions that are not announced to everyone.
Construction and repair can overlap instead of upkeep waiting for completion of the entire mark.
Machine escalation can answer resistance to an offensive overwrite as well as difficulty maintaining an existing mark.
Perceived danger to a neighbouring flag is explicitly made a reason to help and seek peace before the danger reaches one's own.
Restraint may rest on friendship or avoiding needless damage without a preceding settled border.
Giving help can depend on one's own work holding rather than follow from one's own shortage of hands.
An offer of reciprocal defence in exchange for rebuilding help receives a direct pixel pledge.
A shared threat and uncovered sleeping hours are explicitly invoked to justify alliances across time zones.
A call for hands may already name an attack target, so mobilisation and attacking need not be sequential stages.
A proposal to mark an allied flag receives a refusal that explicitly names the alliance as its reason.
An attack proposal is answered by invoking the friendship that makes the target inappropriate.
An invasion call has a reply branch reporting repeated heckling in the rival's chat.
The concepts about too few hands and the negotiated Tango move do not supply a linked shortage-driven relocation.
A report that the flag was completed receives a direct celebration of being first.
The ending celebration receives a timelapse preserving the reported survival of the flag.
A header proposal explicitly reuses an image, but pre-closure commemoration and unanswered successor calls do not require final archiving as their trigger.
The offer-to-disclaimer sequence supports limited representation but does not demonstrate rejection of an agreement's binding authority.
Making revised plans usable depends on returning chat decisions to an accessible public channel.
Revising a shared design requires accounting for active bots that continue defending an earlier target.
